title: Workload Sleuth: continuous batching profile composer
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Build a continuous "workload sleuth" service that profiles request signatures and synthesizes safe per-route batching and caching parameter profiles. The composer will produce conservative initial configs, run dry/shadow applies, and gradually promote changes based on telemetry-driven safety gates.
rationale: Many customers show 15-40% token-cost variance across routes due to suboptimal batching and cache settings. Manual tuning is slow and brittle; a lightweight, continuous profiler + composer can reclaim cost while preserving latency SLOs and reducing operator toil.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Composer outputs per-route profile with concrete parameters (microbatch_size, max_batch_tokens, coalescing_window_ms, cache_prefix_rules). 2) Can perform dry-run and shadow apply without changing live serving. 3) Safe canary rollout pipeline exists with automatic rollback triggers. 4) Verified on 3 internal routes with >=8% token-cost reduction and <5% p95 latency regression relative to baseline.
technical_notes: Profile signal set: arrival_rate(t), interarrival distribution, seq_len histogram, model_variant proportions, kv_cache_hit_rate, cold_start_ratio, p50/p95 latency, error_rate, token_per_request. Composer uses moving-window fingerprints (24h/1h) to detect stable workload clusters. Heuristics include: prefer larger microbatches for steady arrival_rate and high cache_hit_rate; smaller windows for spiky tails. Use simulated token-cost estimator with our kernel latency model to predict cost/latency tradeoffs.
implementation_plan: 1) Inference telemetry extractor (kafka consumer) to normalize request signatures. 2) Workload fingerprint service that emits cluster ids and stability score. 3) Profile composer engine (stateless) that proposes parameter sets ranked by predicted cost savings and safety score. 4) Dry-run executor that simulates batching locally using production traces. 5) Shadow apply and canary orchestrator integrated with rollout controller. 6) Dashboard and alerts (Datadog + Console) for monitoring experiments.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint/clusterer, integration tests hooking into trace replay harness, backtest suite against 30-day historical traces, canary on internal non-critical routes, A/B measurement with rollout controller accounting for sampling noise. Metrics to validate: token_cost_per_1000_requests, p50/p95 latency, error_rate, KV cache hit-rate.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal simulation + unit tests. Stage 1: dry-run mode enabled in staging for two weeks. Stage 2: shadow-apply on 5% of route traffic for 72 hours. Stage 3: incremental canary 5->20->50% with 24h windows and automated rollback thresholds. Stage 4: automatic full promotion when metrics stable for 72h.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback triggers: p95 latency increase >10% absolute or 50ms, error_rate relative increase >2x baseline, token_cost increase >8% for 1h aggregated, infra resource exhaust alarms. Rollback is immediate revert to last known-good profile and creates incident ticket for investigation.
metrics: Primary: token_cost_per_10k_requests (API) Secondary: p50/p95 latency, error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, apply_success_rate, proportion_of_routes_with_profiles, profile_stability_index
risks: 1) Model of cost vs latency may be inaccurate for new model architectures. 2) Fingerprinting could misclassify multi-tenant routes. 3) Safety thresholds tuned too loose -> customer-visible regressions. 4) Rollout controller bugs might cause flapping. Mitigation: conservative defaults, shadow runs, canary automation with human-in-loop for first 30 promotions.
